bombastic

bom-BAS-tik · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Bombastic is high-sounding but with little real meaning -- inflated in language or manner, all grand words and no real substance.

The infomercial host's bombastic promises -- 'this blender will change your life forever!' -- grew more exaggerated with every sentence.

Example

The general's bombastic speech promised total, swift, glorious victory, though it offered no actual plan for achieving any of it.

Bombastic language sounds impressive on the surface -- big words, grand claims -- but falls apart the moment you look for real substance underneath.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

grandiloquent: Grandiloquent targets the words themselves: long, ornate, self-consciously lofty vocabulary chosen to sound learned. Bombastic targets the claims -- talk can be bombastic in plain words if it promises far more than it delivers, and a grandiloquent lecture may still be full of substance.

pompous: Pompous describes the speaker more than the speech -- a self-important manner, treating one's own words as grand pronouncements. Bombastic judges the language itself: high-sounding claims with nothing underneath. A pompous professor may deliver solid facts; bombastic talk collapses when you ask what it actually said.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

understated: presented in a subtle, restrained way

modest: not boastful or exaggerated

Where it sits · how overdone the style becomes — showy → bombastic → overwrought

showy vs. bombastic: Showy describes surfaces built to catch the eye -- flash, glitter, decoration -- a milder failing than bombastic, which inflates the claims themselves.

overwrought vs. bombastic: Overwrought describes speech or writing so excessively elaborate and overdone it goes even further than bombastic.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — bombast

root — bombast: originally, cotton padding used to stuff clothing; later, inflated, empty language (French bombace, from Latin bombax 'cotton')

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: having the qualities of (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Bombastic comes from bombast, which originally meant the cotton padding tailors stuffed into clothing to make it look bigger than it was. Bombastic language is 'padded' the same way -- puffed up and impressive-looking, with nothing solid underneath.

Use the root in a new word: bombast

Word Choice

Bombastic is a criticism, not a compliment -- it targets speech or writing that's all show, with grand-sounding words hiding a lack of real content.
